_comment: Recorded interview answers, keyed by candidate id. Each answer is treated as the source document for interview evidence and re-evaluated against the requirement. C-04 (Rahul) demonstrates both paths: a strong, specific Kubernetes answer that should flip the requirement to met, and a vague Kafka answer that should stay unverified with a follow-up.

C-04.answer: Yes. At Swiggy I deployed our order services on AWS EKS. I owned the Helm charts, configured liveness and readiness probes, and set CPU and memory requests and limits. I ran the rolling deployments myself, and during one production incident a bad rollout was failing health checks, so I rolled it back with kubectl and then added a stricter readiness gate so it could not happen again. I was on the on-call rotation for that cluster for about a year.
Yeah, I've worked with Kafka a bit.
